summary: Montclair Bio walked through their identity boundaries and least-privilege requirements. Main outcomes: agreement to use SAML 2.0 for SSO with SCIM provisioning for groups, scope RBAC around environment tags and service accounts, require KMS integration for enterprise key management, and to validate audit log retention settings for EU data residency. Action items captured and a follow-up configuration session scheduled.
topics: SAML SSO setup and relayState behavior
RBAC model: roles vs resource tags vs org units
Service accounts and machine identity best practices
Audit log retention, export, and EU residency concerns
transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We scheduled 55 minutes to walk through identity and access. Quick intros?
[00:06] Elena: Elena Park, Head of InfoSec at Montclair. I'll drive policy decisions.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Reyes, IT Ops, I'll do the SSO/IdP stuff.
[00:13] Ravi: Ravi Patel, SRE, I'll handle infra integration.
[00:16] Maya: Maya Gonzalez from Legal, just listening for compliance artifacts.
[00:19] Jared: Great. Priya with me is our SE who'll talk through SCIM and RBAC. Priya?
[00:23] Priya: Hi! Quick yes, will demo our console and provisioning flow. I might jump in with a whiteboard sketch.
[00:27] [00:30] Tom: Quick constraint — our IdP is LatticeID (SAML 2.0) hosted in EU, and we require SAML assertions to contain eduPersonPrincipalName and groups claim. We also have a SCIM endpoint for provisioning but the schema is slightly custom.
[00:40] Priya: Okay, good to know. Our SCIM supports custom attribute mappings, we can map groups to role assignments. One question up front: do you want direct group->role mapping or a two-step where groups provision into groups then we map groups to roles?
[00:51] Elena: Prefer the two-step for least-privilege auditing — groups reflect org structure and roles are minimal privilege. Legal also likes distinct role names.
[00:58] Priya: Makes sense. We'll show the mapping patterns. For SAML, our recommended flow is SP-initiated SSO with a metadata exchange; we accept standard NameID formats. We do support RelayState for app deep links but recommend short TTL.
[01:12] Ravi: Any gotchas with assertion size? Our groups list can be long — some teams have 200+ group memberships.
[01:19] Priya: Good flag. We support SCIM for provisioning to avoid huge SAML assertions. If you still include groups in SAML, use a condensed claim or split into role identifiers.
[01:28] Tom: SCIM: our schema has an attribute 'affiliation' for lab vs corporate; can that be mapped?
[01:33] Priya: Yes, custom attributes supported. We'll show the mapping UI and the JSON patch flow. It tolerates 429 backoff hints, rate-limited provisioning flows.
[01:42] [01:45] Elena: On RBAC — our policy is least privilege, separation of duties. We're worried about console privilege escalation and service accounts that have broad scopes. How do you recommend scoping service accounts for model inference?
[01:58] Priya: We recommend scoped service identities per environment (dev/test/prod) with resource-tag-bound roles. Example: inference-prod-runner role only permitted to call /v1/generate on model XYZ in prod clusters. Use short lived tokens for ephemeral workloads.
[02:12] Jared: To add, Redwood supports tenant-level roles plus route-level ACLs. You can bind roles to specific model versions and to dedicated capacity pools.
[02:21] Ravi: Do you emit audit entries for token creation and model invocation with identity context? We need to tie generated logs back to a user/service principal and request_id.
[02:29] Priya: Yes — detailed audit logs include actor, token_id hash, route, model id, input size, latency, and request_id. We can export logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS or to S3/GCS.
[02:40] Maya: Data residency — some payloads contain EU-only PII. We host in EU region but need to ensure key material doesn't leave EU. Can KMS HSM be EU-local?
[02:51] Priya: We integrate with customer-managed KMS, including cloud KMS in region, and support HSM-backed keys. Our private deployment option can be pinned to a customer KMS key and never export plaintext outside the VPC.
[03:05] Elena: For SOC 2 evidence, what artifacts will we get?
[03:08] Jared: We'll provide SOC2 Type II summary, control mappings, encryption configs, RBAC audits, and audit log extracts. We'll redact where necessary.
[03:17] Elena: Good. Also, on role proliferation — we don't want hundreds of roles. We prefer a small set of roles and rely on resource tags for fine-grained access. Does your console support tag-based policies?
[03:27] Priya: Yes, policy expressions can include tags. You can define allow if resource.tag.env == 'prod' and actor.role == 'model-runner'. We also allow time-based constraints for elevated ops windows.
[03:38] Tom: About SCIM provisioning cadence — if a user is deprovisioned in IdP, how quickly will provisioning remove access? We aim for under 5 minutes for deprovision.
[03:48] Priya: Our SCIM hooks support near-real-time provisioning. Typical sync completes under 30s for single changes, dependent on rate limits. We also allow SCIM delta syncs.
[03:55] Ravi: Can we enforce MFA for console admin actions and for service account token issuance?
[03:59] Priya: MFA is enforced at IdP level for human users. For service accounts, short-lived tokens and signing from an internal CA plus approval workflows for elevated scopes are supported. We can also require step-up auth via the IdP.
[04:12] [04:15] Elena: We need proof of encryption in transit and at rest; client's legal team wants an explanation of envelope encryption with customer-managed keys.
[04:25] Priya: Envelope encryption flow: data encrypted with a data encr key (DEK) at service layer, DEK encrypted with your KMS CMK—redwood stores only encrypted DEKs. When private deployment with customer KMS is used, keys never leave your KMS and decrypt happens inside the customer VPC.
[04:40] Maya: How is key rotation handled? Automatic or manual? We have strict rotation windows (90 days).
[04:45] Priya: We support key rotation via KMS versioning. For envelope encryption, rotating the CMK rewraps new DEKs; we provide a rotation playbook and can script rewrap tasks with minimal downtime.
[04:57] Jared: On audit logs retention and access: you mentioned EU residency constraints — we can store audit logs in EU-only S3 and provide log search UI inside EU. Also exportable to your SIEM if that lives in EU.
[05:10] Elena: Very important. Also want proof that PII isn't used for model training or telemetry.
[05:15] Jared: Our data handling policy forbids using customer prompt content for model training. We can add contractual clauses and provide controls for telemetry and scrubbing.
[05:24] Ravi: About RBAC drift — do you support policy versioning or policy-as-code integration?
[05:29] Priya: We have an API to manage policies and version them. You can store policies as JSON in Git and push via CI. We'll also show a diff UI for policy changes.
[05:38] Tom: For SAML metadata exchange — can you accept signed metadata and do metadata rotation?
[05:42] Priya: Yes, SP metadata supports signing and key rotation. We recommend rotating keys every quarter. Our metadata endpoint uses https and we can provide both entityDescriptors.
[05:52] [06:00] Elena: A hypothetical: a researcher leaves the lab but still has active tokens used by long-running jobs. How do you recommend handling token revocation?
[06:10] Priya: Short TTL tokens plus revocation lists. We support immediate revocation of API keys and active sessions on SCIM deprovision or via the admin console. For long-running jobs, use workload identity federation to ensure tokens are ephemeral.
[06:24] Ravi: Any known limitations when integrating with on-prem IdPs behind an IdP proxy?
[06:29] Priya: If the IdP is not reachable outbound from Redwood hosted plane, you'll need SAML proxy or to use our private deployment. The proxy must support SAML HTTP-POST and Metadata exchange.
[06:41] Tom: We're evaluating between hosted and private. Private gives us full KMS control, hosted is faster. Any cost or SLA differences we should know?
[06:48] Jared: Dedicated/private has different pricing—private includes infra and support fees and offers stronger SLAs and data residency guarantees. We can send a pricing comparison.
[06:57] Maya: Legal wants an audit log extract sample for access reviews and one example paging export.
[07:03] Priya: We'll attach a sample CSV export and show the fields: timestamp, actor, action, resource, model_id, request_id, ip, region.
[07:12] [07:15] Jared: Quick recap — next steps: Jared send SAML metadata template + SOC2 pack, Priya send RBAC examples and SCIM mapping demo, Elena to share attribute requirements and list of service accounts. Schedule follow-up config call. Anything else?
[07:29] Elena: Please include SOC2 control numbers that map to identity and access controls.
[07:33] Jared: Will do.
[07:35] Tom: We'll aim to get our IdP metadata and a small test user by the 10th.
[07:40] [07:45] Maya: One last compliance note — retention windows: we need 7 years for some audit trails, can you support that?
[07:51] Priya: Long-term retention is possible via log archival to your S3 bucket; our UI may keep recent logs for 90/180 days but full archive can be kept longer in your storage.
[08:03] Jared: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and docs.
[08:08] [END]
